pairs.q: *Achaian.* Son of Peleus and a sea-goddess, leader of the Myrmidons; his anger is the subject of the poem.
*Achaian.* Son of Atreus, king of Mykenai and lord of men, commander of the whole host.
*Achaian.* Son of Atreus, king of Lakedaimon and Helen's husband; he nearly kills Paris in single combat.
*Achaian.* Son of Laertes, king of Ithaka, known for his cunning; he goes on the night raid with Diomedes.
*Achaian.* Son of Telamon, a huge man with a shield like a wall; he fights Hektor in a duel that ends in a draw.
*Achaian.* Son of Tydeus, lord of Argos; in his great day of fighting he wounds Aphrodite and Ares.
*Achaian.* Aged king of Pylos, full of long advice and stories of the deeds of his youth.
*Achaian.* Son of Menoitios and dearest companion of Achilleus; he fights in Achilleus' armor and is killed by Hektor.
*Achaian.* Achilleus' old tutor; on the embassy he tells the story of Meleagros.
*Achaian.* The captive woman awarded to Achilleus and taken by Agamemnon; she mourns over Patroklos.
*Achaian.* Agamemnon's captive, daughter of Apollo's priest; Odysseus returns her to her father to end the plague.
*Trojan.* Eldest son of Priam and Hekabe, husband of Andromache, the chief defender of the city.
*Trojan.* Aged king of Troy; he comes by night to ransom his son's body and kisses the hands of Achilleus.
*Trojan.* Queen of Troy; she leads the women's offering of a robe to Athene and begs her son from the wall to come inside.
*Trojan.* Infant son of Hektor, frightened by the horsehair crest on his father's helmet; his father calls him Skamandrios.
*Trojan.* Son of Priam who carried off Helen; Aphrodite snatches him away from his duel with Menelaos.
*In Troy.* Daughter of Zeus and wife of Menelaos, taken from Lakedaimon; from the wall she names the Achaian leaders for Priam.
*Trojan.* Son of Anchises and Aphrodite, leader of the Dardanians; one of the only Trojans to survive the war; Poseidon rescues him from Achilleus.
*Trojan.* A spy who goes out at night in a wolfskin; Odysseus and Diomedes catch and kill him.
*Trojan ally.* Son of Zeus and leader of the Lykians, killed by Patroklos; Sleep and Death carry his body home.
*Immortal.* Son of Kronos, father of gods and men, who grants Thetis' prayer to honor her son.
*Immortal.* Queen of the gods, wife and sister of Zeus, who hates Troy; she lulls her husband to sleep on Ida.
*Immortal.* The grey-eyed daughter of Zeus, who grabs Achilleus by the hair to stop him from drawing his sword on Agamemnon.
*Immortal.* Phoibos the archer, whose arrows bring the plague; he strikes Patroklos from behind.
*Immortal.* Goddess of love and mother of Aineias; Diomedes wounds her in the hand.
*Immortal.* The god of war, who fights for the Trojans; Athene knocks him down with a boundary stone.
*Immortal.* The earth-shaker, brother of Zeus and lord of the sea, who rallies the Achaians while Zeus sleeps.
*Immortal.* A sea-goddess and mother of Achilleus, who asks Zeus to give the Trojans the upper hand.
*Immortal.* Argeïphontes, the guide who escorts Priam through the Achaian camp at night.
*Immortal.* The female messenger of the gods.
*Immortal.* The huntress, Apollo's sister; Hera boxes her ears with her own bow.
